sources.title: Kimi Code What's New — K2.8 Preview, September 11, 2026
sources.evidence: Reopened on October 27, 2026. The September 11 K2.8 release describes an in-place kimi-for-coding upgrade, improved coding/thinking efficiency and 1M context, but names no base model and gives no total or active parameter count. Later entries through the October 23 K3.1 launch do not add a K2.8 size or lineage disclosure.

sources.title: Kimi Code Model Configuration
sources.evidence: Reopened the current six-ID table on October 27, 2026. It maps kimi-for-coding to K2.8 Preview with 1048576 context, image/video input and low/high/max reasoning. The table attributes 2.8T to K3 and 3T-class to K3.1 Pro; the separate K2.8 column contains no size or architectural lineage. It documents native Responses/Chat Completions/Anthropic protocols and thinking-off routing.

sources.title: Kimi Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Sections 4.6 and 5 retain Moonshot AI service rights and restrict reverse engineering of service models and unauthorized copying or sublicensing; support a proprietary service classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: Moonshot AI official Hugging Face model inventory
sources.evidence: Fresh direct API read on October 27, 2026 returned 19 official repositories, including Kimi-K3 and Kimi-K2.7-Code, with no K2.8 Preview repository or model card. This inventory is a search aid, not proof of a parameter count.

sources.title: Kimi-K3 official model card
sources.evidence: Reopened the model card and fetched its full README on October 27, 2026: K3 is nominally 2.8T total / 104B activated, with MoE, KDA, Attention Residuals and a 401M MoonViT-V2 encoder. The full README contains no K2.8 mention or developer statement connecting K2.8 to this architecture.

sources.title: Kimi-K2.7-Code official model card
sources.evidence: Reopened the model card and fetched its full README on October 27, 2026: K2.7 Code is built upon K2.6 and explicitly shares K2.5/K2.6 architecture; it reports nominal 1T total / 32B activated MoE parameters and a 400M MoonViT encoder. The full README contains no K2.8 mention. Its explicit earlier-model lineage does not extend to K2.8.

sources.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
sources.evidence: Reopened on October 27, 2026. The technical blog explicitly identifies K3.1 Pro as post-trained from K3 with increased post-training compute. Its full text contains no K2.8 mention, parameter specification or base-model mapping; that documented lineage belongs to K3.1 Pro.

sources.title: Kimi Code Built-in Tools
sources.evidence: Documents agent-selected tool calls for file reading/editing, shell execution and web access; multimodal tools send images/video to models with matching input capabilities.

sources.title: Kimi Code SDK model provider
sources.evidence: Official SDK provider defaults to the kimi-for-coding model ID, connecting the documented K2.8 route with the Kimi provider implementation.

sources.title: Kimi provider request/response adapter
sources.evidence: Official provider accepts tool schemas, sends tool calls, and parses function tool_calls in regular and streaming model responses; handles textual message content.

sources.title: Kimi Code Chinese release history — K2.8 Preview and later updates
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 read confirms the September 11 Chinese announcement describes an unchanged service ID, improved coding/agent performance and thinking efficiency versus K2.7 Code, adjustable reasoning and 1M context. It does not call K2.8 a fine-tune/post-trained version of K2.7, disclose total/active counts, or state that the architecture was preserved. Later updates through October 23 add no K2.8 disclosure.

sources.title: Kimi Research Blog — current research index
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 read lists the October 24 K3.1 Pro article, K3, K2.6, K2.5 and earlier research. No K2.8 article or technical report is listed. Used with targeted English/Chinese searches for K2.8 parameters, architecture, post-training, base-model lineage, pruning and distillation; no newer first-party K2.8 size or lineage disclosure was located.

name.note: K2.8 Preview is the official version name; Kimi is the product/model brand.

developer.note: First-party release documentation and service ownership identify Moonshot AI.

family.note: Normalized catalog family follows the official K2.8 name; this naming classification does not establish shared K2 checkpoint specifications.

release_date.note: Explicit dated public full-rollout entry. Targeted earlier-date/beta searches in English and Chinese and the preceding changelog entries found no earlier primary K2.8 release date; retain this earliest verified date, without claiming it excludes an earlier limited test.

open_weights.note: The documented release is hosted access; the official 19-model repository inventory has no K2.8 checkpoint. No separate weight release was located as of this review.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted release under restrictive service terms. No K2.8 open-weight license is established; sibling or client-code licenses do not apply.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found neither a developer-published nominal K2.8 total nor an explicit named-base/post-training relationship. K2.7 Code has a supported nominal 1T total, but its documented K2.5/K2.6 architectural lineage does not name K2.8; replacing its serving ID and improving its performance are insufficient to inherit size. K3 is separately specified at 2.8T. No K2.8 statement establishes preserved expert, attention or vision structure. This null reflects missing size/lineage evidence, not a requirement for an exact tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh review separately found no K2.8 activated-parameter figure or routing/architecture disclosure supporting one. K2.7 Code reports nominal 32B activated and K3 reports 104B, but no developer statement makes K2.8 a post-trained version of either or establishes unchanged experts, attention and vision components. Thinking-effort settings and fewer reasoning tokens do not identify the parameters active per token. A supported nominal active count would be accepted without a tensor census.

architecture.note: Fresh parameter-lineage review leaves architecture undisclosed. The English/Chinese rollout, model table, research index and sibling cards establish no K2.8 base-model relationship or structural continuity. No K2.8 disclosure of expert topology, attention changes, pruning, distillation or encoder structure was located; absence of such a disclosure cannot establish unchanged architecture. The K2 name and unchanged service ID alone do not support a MoE/MLA/KDA inference.

context_window.note: Exact maximum in the K2.8 Preview column, measured in tokens.

modalities.note: Model table explicitly lists image/video input; the mapped provider implements text messages and textual responses. No audio or generated-media output claim is made.

reasoning.note: Explicit low/high/max thinking levels, default max. Optional no-thinking service does not make this a non-reasoning model.

tool_call.note: Exact model route is supported by the official coding-agent provider, which accepts tool schemas and emits/parses function tool calls; first-party agent documentation explains execution.

Kimi Research Blog — current research index

patch.notes: K2.8 Preview is the Kimi Code model behind kimi-for-coding. September 11, 2026 is the explicit full-rollout date and earliest verified release date in this audit. The October 27 parameter re-audit reopened English/Chinese release notes, the current model table, official model inventory, sibling model cards and the newer K3.1 Pro technical blog; targeted English/Chinese searches and the current research index located no K2.8 nominal size or explicit named-base/post-training lineage. Total and active parameters therefore remain undisclosed. K2.7 Code explicitly reports 1T/32B and K3 reports 2.8T/104B, but neither card maps its architecture to K2.8. The unchanged service ID and qualitative comparisons do not establish that experts, attention or vision structure were preserved, so architecture also remains undisclosed. Supported nominal counts or documented lineage would suffice; an exact checkpoint census is not required. Reasoning is optional and adjustable. No K2.8 weights were present in the fresh 19-repository official inventory; sibling weight licenses do not transfer.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains null/undisclosed total and active counts after fresh primary-source review and targeted English/Chinese searches. No K2.8 nominal size or explicit base/post-training lineage was located. The documented 1T/32B K2.7 Code and 2.8T/104B K3 specifications cannot be inherited from endpoint replacement or performance comparisons; structural continuity is unestablished. Added Chinese release-history and current research-index evidence, refreshed prior parameter sources, and made both null patch values explicit. Unrelated audited fields are preserved.
